description: A pathway diploma run by Bond University College, about eight months (two semesters) full-time, covering roughly eight first-year business subjects alongside intensive academic skills work in essay writing, critical reading, referencing and time management, taught in small classes reserved for diploma students. On completion, students get guaranteed entry with about 80 credit points of advanced standing into most Bond undergraduate degrees, including Business, Commerce, International Hotel and Tourism Management and Sport Management, starting from third semester. It suits students who do not meet direct entry for a Bond bachelor, or who want a supported first year before joining the main degree. Bond College runs the same model in Arts, Built Environment, Health Sciences and Legal Studies, plus a one-year Creative Design diploma.

A Bond University College pathway diploma, about eight months (two semesters) full-time, made up of around eight first-year subjects across humanities and social sciences, taught with extra academic skills support in small diploma-only classes. On completion, students receive guaranteed entry into most Bond undergraduate arts and social science degrees with roughly 80 credit points of advanced standing, joining the bachelor from third semester. It suits students who do not meet direct entry for a Bond bachelor or who want a supported first year. Bond College runs the same model in Business, Built Environment, Health Sciences and Legal Studies, plus a one-year Creative Design diploma.

A Bond University College pathway diploma, about eight months (two semesters) full-time, covering around eight first-year subjects in architecture, construction and the built environment, with extra academic skills support in small diploma-only classes. On completion, students get guaranteed entry into Bond's built environment bachelors, such as the Bachelor of Design in Architecture or construction degrees, with roughly 80 credit points of advanced standing, joining from third semester. It suits students who do not meet direct entry or who want a supported first year before the main degree. Bond College runs the same model across Arts, Business, Health Sciences and Legal Studies, plus a one-year Creative Design diploma.

A Bond University College pathway diploma, about eight months (two semesters) full-time, made up of around eight first-year subjects across health and biomedical sciences, taught with extra academic skills support in small diploma-only classes. On completion, students receive guaranteed entry into Bond health sciences and biomedical bachelors with roughly 80 credit points of advanced standing, joining the degree from third semester. Progression into programs with their own selection process, such as medicine or physiotherapy, is not guaranteed by the diploma. It suits students who do not meet direct entry or who want a supported first year. Bond College runs the same model across Arts, Business, Built Environment and Legal Studies, plus a one-year Creative Design diploma.

A Bond University College pathway diploma, about eight months (two semesters) full-time, covering around eight first-year subjects in law and legal studies, taught with extra academic skills support in small diploma-only classes. On completion, students receive guaranteed entry into Bond's law and legal studies bachelors with roughly 80 credit points of advanced standing, joining from third semester. It suits students who do not meet direct entry for a Bond law degree or who want a supported first year before the main program. Bond College runs the same model across Arts, Business, Built Environment and Health Sciences, plus a one-year Creative Design diploma.

A one-year Bond University College pathway diploma in creative and communication design, longer than Bond's other pathway diplomas, covering foundation design subjects alongside academic skills support in small diploma-only classes. On completion, students receive guaranteed entry into Bond's design and creative media bachelors with advanced standing, joining the degree partway through rather than starting again. It suits students who do not meet direct entry or who want a supported, portfolio-building first year before the main degree. Bond College runs a shorter eight-month version of this model in Arts, Business, Built Environment, Health Sciences and Legal Studies.

A pre-university course run by Bond University College for students who have finished school but do not yet meet the academic requirements for direct bachelor entry, including many international students whose qualifications sit below Australian Year 12. It runs about nine to ten months and combines academic subjects with English and study skills, taught in small classes. On completion at the required standard, students progress into the first year of a Bond bachelor's degree. It suits school leavers who need a recognised bridging year before starting an undergraduate degree at Bond.

A short preparation course, roughly one semester, run by Bond University College for students who need to build English and academic skills before starting one of Bond's pathway diplomas. It focuses on academic writing, reading, study techniques and the language demands of university study, in small classes. On completion at the required standard, students move into a Bond College diploma, and from there into a bachelor's degree. It suits students who are close to but not yet at the entry standard for a Bond diploma.

An APAC-accredited conversion qualification that gives graduates the equivalent of the first three years of the psychology training sequence. It is for people whose bachelor's degree was in another field, or whose psychology degree is more than ten years old, or psychology graduates who need stronger grades to progress to the accredited fourth year. On Bond's three-semester calendar, students with a cognate background finish in about eight months and others in a year. Completion makes a student honours-equivalent and eligible to apply for the accredited fourth year, after which further postgraduate study and supervised practice lead toward registration as a psychologist. The diploma itself does not confer any registration. It suits career changers committed to the full psychology pathway.

A one-year pathway diploma delivered by UC College over three trimesters at the Bruce campus, worth 24 credit points. It combines first-year business units in management, economics, business decision-making and communication with a required Academic English unit and explicit academic-skills teaching. On completion, students progress directly into the second year of a range of University of Canberra bachelor's degrees, including Business majors, Politics and International Relations and Government. Entry requires IELTS 5.5 or equivalent. It suits students, particularly international students, who do not meet direct entry or who want a supported, English-strengthening first year. UC College runs the same model in Communication, Design, Health, Information Technology and Science.

A one-year pathway diploma delivered by UC College over three trimesters at the Bruce campus, worth 24 credit points, combining first-year communication and media units with a required Academic English unit and academic-skills teaching. On completion, students move directly into the second year of University of Canberra communication and media bachelor's degrees. Entry requires IELTS 5.5 or equivalent. It suits students, particularly international students, who do not meet direct entry or who want a supported first year with built-in English development. UC College runs the same model in Business, Design, Health, Information Technology and Science.

A one-year pathway diploma delivered by UC College over three trimesters at the Bruce campus, worth 24 credit points, combining first-year design studio and theory units with a required Academic English unit and academic-skills teaching. On completion, students progress directly into the second year of University of Canberra design bachelor's degrees. Entry requires IELTS 5.5 or equivalent. It suits students, particularly international students, who do not meet direct entry or who want a supported first year while building English and studio skills. UC College runs the same model in Business, Communication, Health, Information Technology and Science.

A one-year pathway diploma delivered by UC College over three trimesters at the Bruce campus, worth 24 credit points, combining first-year health science units with a required Academic English unit and academic-skills teaching. On completion, students move directly into the second year of a range of University of Canberra health bachelor's degrees. Progression into programs with their own selection process, such as nursing or medical imaging, may have additional requirements. Entry requires IELTS 5.5 or equivalent. It suits students, particularly international students, who do not meet direct entry or who want a supported first year. UC College runs the same model in Business, Communication, Design, Information Technology and Science.

A one-year pathway diploma delivered by UC College over three trimesters at the Bruce campus, worth 24 credit points, combining first-year information technology units in programming, systems and networks with a required Academic English unit and academic-skills teaching. On completion, students progress directly into the second year of University of Canberra IT and computing bachelor's degrees. Entry requires IELTS 5.5 or equivalent. It suits students, particularly international students, who do not meet direct entry or who want a supported first year with built-in English development. UC College runs the same model in Business, Communication, Design, Health and Science.

A one-year pathway diploma delivered by UC College over three trimesters at the Bruce campus, worth 24 credit points, combining first-year science units in biology, chemistry and quantitative methods with a required Academic English unit and academic-skills teaching. On completion, students move directly into the second year of University of Canberra science bachelor's degrees. Entry requires IELTS 5.5 or equivalent. It suits students, particularly international students, who do not meet direct entry or who want a supported first year while strengthening English and laboratory skills. UC College runs the same model in Business, Communication, Design, Health and Information Technology.

A one-year pre-university course delivered by UC College at the Bruce campus for international students who have completed the equivalent of Year 11 but do not meet direct entry to a University of Canberra bachelor's degree. The curriculum is pitched at Australian Year 12 level: 12 units across English, mathematics, technology and humanities and society, worth 36 credit points over three terms, developing both English proficiency and university study skills. Entry requires IELTS 5.5 with no band below 5.0 and a minimum age of 17. On successful completion, students gain entry into the first year of most UC undergraduate degrees. It suits international students who need a recognised foundation year before starting university in Australia.

A fee-free 15-week enabling program at Murdoch's Perth campus for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students who want to move into an undergraduate degree without the usual prerequisites, starting from around Year 10 level. Study is on campus, full-time over four days a week or part-time across two semesters, in classes capped at 30 for close support. The curriculum covers academic writing, referencing, essay structure, scientific method and study skills such as time management and critical thinking. Because it is classed as full-time study, students may be eligible for Centrelink payments. On completion at the required standard, students qualify to apply for entry to a Murdoch undergraduate degree. It suits First Nations students, including mature-age applicants, returning to or entering formal study.

A four-week intensive enabling course at Murdoch's Perth campus, running full-time on weekdays in January, for domestic students who just missed direct entry, typically recent school leavers with an ATAR in the low-to-mid 60s or strong general subject results. On successful completion it lets students apply directly for Murdoch undergraduate degrees that require a selection rank of 70 or below. It is not a guaranteed pathway into competitive programs such as nursing. It suits near-miss applicants who want a fast route into study in the same year rather than waiting for a full semester-long enabling course.

Murdoch's general enabling course, a 14-week program for both school leavers and mature-age applicants who do not have a competitive ATAR or recent formal study. It builds academic writing, research, referencing and study skills, and can be taken on campus or in a more flexible format. On successful completion, students receive a selection rank equivalent to 70, which qualifies them to apply for most Murdoch undergraduate degrees. Entry into programs with their own additional selection criteria is not guaranteed. It suits people who need a single semester of university preparation before starting a bachelor's degree.

A community-based enabling program at Murdoch aimed at adult learners returning to study, focused on building academic literacy, writing and study skills in a supportive setting. On successful completion, students receive a selection rank equivalent to 70, qualifying them to apply for most Murdoch undergraduate degrees; entry to programs with their own selection criteria is not guaranteed. It suits mature-age people who left formal education some time ago and want a supported route back into university study.

An enabling pathway at Murdoch designed specifically for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students who want to study veterinary science but do not have a science background. It builds the foundation science and academic skills needed for the degree and provides a supported route into Murdoch's veterinary science program, which is one of only a small number in Australia. It suits First Nations students committed to a veterinary career who need a science bridging year first.

A pathway at Murdoch for high-achieving Year 12 students who want an alternative route into a university degree. Rather than relying only on an ATAR, students take Murdoch study while still at school and, on meeting the requirements, receive a selection rank equivalent to 70 for entry to most Murdoch undergraduate degrees. It suits current secondary students who want to start building university credit and secure a pathway before they finish school.
